description: A hosting decision for a radio archive that has the right shape and passes the trace check, and is wrong: criteria from nowhere, two options, the vendor's own page as evidence, an upload test for a download problem, and arithmetic that turns $473 a month into $23.45.

defects.tell: Popularity 40% and developer experience 30% come from no measure; cost, which M1 makes a hard limit of $60, is only a 30% weight; M2 (links that never change) is not a criterion at all
only the two vendors that came up; doing nothing, the station's own NAS, and combining (masters on the NAS, a host for serving) were never options
transfer out is 5,000 GB x $0.09 = $450, not 0.09 x 5 = $0.45; CloudA is $473 a month, nearly eight times M1. CloudB is $55, because free downloads stop at three times the stored volume
the only source on quality is CloudA's own marketing page, including its comparison with CloudB
the speed test uploads a 2 MB file from the office; the use is listeners downloading 60 MB shows on phones

recorded as two-way, but CloudA serves only from its own domain, so every feed and blog link would carry CloudA's URL and leaving would break M2: a one-way door with no exit, no approval and a revisit condition that never fires

control.tell: the audio format decision is done right: criteria dated before the comparison and tied to measures, four options, a blind ABX test and the apps' own support pages as independent evidence, the arithmetic shown, and an exit through the FLAC masters. A report that faults it is inventing.
